name: Bashluth
title: Temple worker who returned from exile
summary: Bashluth (also known as Bazlut or Bazlit) was the ancestor of a family of temple servants (Nethinim) who returned to Jerusalem from the Babylonian exile under Zerubbabel's leadership. His descendants are mentioned among those who contributed to the rebuilding of the temple and Jewish community life in Judah.

keyEvents.title: Listed among the temple servants who returned
keyEvents.description: Bashluth's descendants are listed among the Nethinim families (temple servants) who returned from the Babylonian exile to Jerusalem under Zerubbabel's leadership.

keyEvents.title: Re-listed in Nehemiah's account
keyEvents.description: Bashluth's family is mentioned again in Nehemiah's parallel list of those who returned from exile, confirming their role as temple servants.

keyEvents.title: The role of temple servants in the rebuilding
keyEvents.description: The temple servants, including Bashluth's descendants, settled in Jerusalem and surrounding towns to support the rebuilding and operation of the temple.

keyEvents.title: Identification among Israel's returnees
keyEvents.description: Baslu's family was among those who could prove their lineage and belonging to the Jewish people when they returned from Babylon.
